args.title: checkout-api failing health checks after v2.3.1 deploy — rolled back to v2.3.0
args.summary: checkout-api v2.3.1 (latest deploy) was failing health checks in all production regions (us-east, us-west, eu-west) with an error rate of ~18%. Release history shows v2.3.1-rc and v2.3.1 both unhealthy; the most recent healthy release was v2.3.0. Rolled checkout-api back to v2.3.0 in all production regions; rollback completed and verified in us-east, us-west, eu-west. Follow-up: investigate root cause of the v2.3.1 failure before re-deploying.

trace.final:
I rolled checkout-api back to v2.3.0 in all three regions, and it's passing health checks again. I also opened SEV2 incident INC-0001, which paged the on-call engineer.

- **What was wrong:** v2.3.1 was running in us-east, us-west and eu-west, failing health checks with an 18% error rate.
- **Which release I picked:** v2.3.0 is the most recent healthy release. The deploy history wasn't listed in order, so I sorted it by sequence number. Both releases after v2.3.0 were unhealthy: v2.3.1-rc and v2.3.1.
- **Rollback:** finished in all three regions. The service now shows as healthy, with the error rate down to 0.2%.
- **Incident:** INC-0001 says the problem was the v2.3.1 deploy, describes the rollback and asks for the root cause to be found before v2.3.1 is deployed again.

content.text: The deployment list isn't in sequence order, so I sorted it by seq: v2.2.9 (healthy), v2.3.0 (healthy), v2.3.1-rc (unhealthy), v2.3.1 (unhealthy, current). The most recent healthy release is v2.3.0.
